public_rationale: OpenAI's March 14, 2023 disclosure stated that jailbreaks could still make GPT-4 generate content violating its usage guidelines [e1]. This supports the claim's ordinary reading that adversarial inputs could still expose failures at release [e1]. OpenAI also reported improved safety relative to GPT-3.5, alongside those remaining failures [e1].
limitations: The disclosure does not measure the prevalence of remaining jailbreak failures or performance on a formally defined out-of-distribution benchmark [e1].
Adversarial safeguard failures do not establish failures across every class of unusual input [e1].
The packet provides OpenAI's disclosure without independent replication.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Outliers remain a problem for GPT-4.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that unusual or adversarial inputs still expose failures in GPT-4. This does not assert that every unusual input fails.
The target is the March 2023 release state, through the post date. I use March month-to-date as the latest public reporting window.
A formal statistical definition of out-of-distribution performance would require a specified reference distribution, which Marcus does not provide.
criteria.support_condition: Release-era evidence documents failures on unusual or adversarial inputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Release-era evaluations establish reliable handling of the relevant unusual inputs and show that the alleged failure cases do not apply to GPT-4.
